correctness.rationale: Polar differentiation gives theta-dot=1 and a linear inverse-square equation. The explicit periodic particular solution reduces at criticality to (2/lambda)sin^2; positivity of its exact homogeneous perturbation is necessary and sufficient for forward completeness, with radii growing exactly exponentially at fixed angular phases. These samples are not local maxima because the radius has positive derivative there. Exact disk-chord integration gives the area law; bounded-convergence phase averaging yields the radial occupation survival. The rotated Cartesian coordinate makes the forward-complete set precisely a strip bounded by invariant straight lines. The strict boundary, zero equilibrium, both h signs and every lambda>0 are included. Finite rational and numerical checker tests alone are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: At the natural disappearance of a homogeneous-rigid limit cycle through infinity, the existence of nonzero forward-complete but unbounded trajectories is a substantive boundary phenomenon. The theorem describes their complete-versus-finite-escape planar initial-data geometry, a sharp invariant-line strip and a linear area coefficient within large disks, and an exact original-time Pareto occupation law with divergent mean. These quantitative invariants are motivated by the infinity polycycle and do not claim new integrability or a generic global classification.
